_comment: Shared TypeScript config for every Node service under services/.
A SIBLING of tsconfig.base.json, not a child. That file is the browser /
Svelte profile — DOM + DOM.Iterable in lib, types: ['svelte'],
allowImportingTsExtensions, isolatedModules — for the federated members
under apps/ and the host in shell/. This one is the Node profile: ES2022
only, types: ['node'], and noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters on. Making
one extend the other would take five override-to-undo entries and would
document the relationship as a lie. They are two profiles, not a profile
and a variant.
Before this file, 10 of the 11 service tsconfig.json files were
byte-identical (md5 540460bd93f2916e7ccfd45e30e6a7bd) and none of them
extended anything — the same drift tsconfig.base.json was written to stop
for the apps, caught one step earlier. The services had not yet split into
variants, which is exactly why folding them was still a no-op.
services/decile-mcp is the one service that legitimately differs: it is
compiled to dist/ and started with node, where the other ten are run
through tsx. It extends this file and overrides only the emit/module axis.
services/deploy-relay has NO tsconfig.json and needs none — its only
source file is api/railway.js, a single Vercel function in plain
JavaScript. 11 of 12 is the correct count, not a gap. Recorded here so it
is not re-raised as an open item by the next codebase-graph diff.
Only compilerOptions live here. include/exclude deliberately stay in each
service: TypeScript resolves those paths relative to the file they are
WRITTEN in, not the one doing the extending, so a shared 'src/**/*.ts'
would resolve to '<root>/src/**/*.ts' and every service would compile zero
files — silently, and green. tsconfig.base.json records learning this the
hard way; do not re-learn it.
